originalTitle: US stocks: S&P closes at record high as soft jobs report eases rate-hike concerns
simplifiedContent: The US stock market had a great day on Friday, with the S&P (a group of major companies) reaching its highest point ever. This happened because there were more job losses than expected, which made investors think that the Federal Reserve (the group that controls interest rates) might not raise interest rates in September. This is good news for the stock market, and combined with strong earnings reports from companies, it helped push the market up. Additionally, oil prices went down, which helps reduce fears of inflation (when prices rise too quickly). This all helped to boost the stock market to a new high.

originalTitle: Market cuts odds of Fed hike after jobs data, but economists still see case for tightening
simplifiedContent: Recently, the number of new jobs created in July was lower than expected, which has made people less sure that the Federal Reserve will raise interest rates next month. Because of this, investors are now guessing that a rate increase is less likely to happen. Some officials at the Federal Reserve still think that interest rates should be raised to help control inflation, but others are not so sure. The Federal Reserve is watching inflation closely to decide what to do with interest rates. This matters because a change in interest rates can affect the overall economy and the stock market.

originalTitle: Dollar falls against yen, euro as weak US jobs data clouds Fed outlook
simplifiedContent: The value of the US dollar went down compared to other major currencies, like the yen and euro, on Friday. This happened because the US job market didn't do as well as expected in July, with more people losing jobs than anticipated. Even though the unemployment rate (the percentage of people without jobs) actually decreased, fewer people were participating in the workforce, which is a concern. This news makes it less clear what the Federal Reserve (the US central bank) will do with interest rates in the future. As a result, investors lost confidence in the US dollar, causing its value to drop.

originalTitle: Short-Term Treasuries Cap Biggest Weekly Rally Since May on Data
simplifiedContent: Here's what's happening: the US government's short-term debt, called Treasuries, had a big increase in value this week. This happened because a recent report on jobs in the US was weaker than expected, which made investors think that the Federal Reserve (the group that controls interest rates) might not raise interest rates as much as they thought. As a result, the value of short-term Treasuries went up a lot, having their best week since May. This matters because it shows how investors are reacting to new information and changing their expectations about what the Federal Reserve will do next. The increase in value is a significant move, indicating a shift in investor sentiment.

originalTitle: Treasury yields fall as jobs report dashes hike bets
simplifiedContent: The US government's bond prices, known as Treasury yields, have gone down. This happened after a recent jobs report was released, which showed that the job market isn't as strong as people thought. As a result, investors are now less likely to think that interest rates will be increased soon. This change in expectations caused the Treasury yields to fall. The drop in Treasury yields means that investors can now buy government bonds at a lower return, which could impact other investments in the market.

originalTitle: Gold hits seven-week high as weak US jobs data dents rate hike bets
simplifiedContent: The price of gold has reached its highest point in seven weeks. This happened because the latest jobs data from the US was weaker than expected. As a result, investors are less likely to think that interest rates will be increased soon. This matters because when interest rates are low, gold is often more attractive to investors, which can drive up its price. The weak jobs data and potential delay in interest rate increases are the reasons why gold is currently doing well.
